clue.text: His padre could be a rabbi

definitions.text: His padre could be a rabbi

indicators.note: could be says the letters of the two words may turn into something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone muses that their own chaplain might in fact be a Jewish religious leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' signals an anagram of HISPADRE. The whole clue doubles as the definition: a rabbi might well be of Spanish-Portuguese Jewish descent.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sephardic Jew descends from the Jewish communities of Spain and Portugal, and a rabbi may belong to that tradition.

clue.text: Lambert takes the cake

explanation.surface: A man named Lambert wins the prize, or eats the pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: Lambert Simnel was a pretender to the English throne in 1487; a simnel cake is a British fruit cake eaten at Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambert Simnel was a Tudor-era pretender, and a simnel is a marzipan-topped fruit loaf baked for Easter.

clue.text: How the young can be taken for a ride

definitions.text: How the young can be taken for a ride

parts.words: How the young can be taken for a ride
parts.note: taken for a ride suggests being cheated, but here a small child is literally carried on someone's back

explanation.surface: Gullible youngsters are easily deceived.
explanation.definitionFit: Children are often carried on an adult's shoulders and back, piggyback style.

clue.text: Attribute to a note about Father Time

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go around the next

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone assigns a musical note to Father Time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father Time' reads as the one allegorical figure with scythe and hourglass, but its two words give separate pieces; 'about' puts the A and N round the father word.
explanation.definitionFit: An apanage, in an extended sense, is a natural adjunct or characteristic property of something.

clue.text: Dig into free meal in river setting

indicators.note: setting means the river forms a frame around the other piece

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
LV is a luncheon voucher, a British meal ticket given free by employers

explanation.surface: Digging into a free lunch beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: LV, a luncheon voucher, is a British coupon given to workers for a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: To delve is to dig, literally or by research.

clue.text: Platoon is holding the line push forward

indicators.note: is holding means one piece clasps the other within it

parts.note: PL is the military abbreviation for platoon
a line is a cord or rope

explanation.surface: A platoon keeps its position in the line while being urged to advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the line' looks like the military front, but here it is a rope, held between P and L.
explanation.definitionFit: To propel something is to drive or thrust it onwards.

clue.text: Reinvest the compensation?

explanation.surface: Putting money back in as a form of compensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reinvest' is read as invest again in the old sense of clothe: to re-dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest once meant to clothe, so to clothe again is re-dress; and redress is reparation for a wrong.

clue.text: Misrepresent 1p as a foreign coin

indicators.note: misrepresent means the letters are presented wrongly, in a new order

parts.note: the numeral 1 stands as the letter I, with P beside it

explanation.surface: Passing a British penny off as foreign currency.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 is read as the letter I, so 'Misrepresent' turns IPAS into PAIS, then A follows; aptly, the coin is a hundredth of a rupee, a 'penny'.
explanation.definitionFit: A paisa is a small coin of India and Pakistan, one hundredth of a rupee.

clue.text: Applies handle — it helps to transmit power

parts.note: to lay paint on is to apply it
a haft is the handle of a knife or tool

explanation.surface: Someone puts a handle on a machine part that conveys power.
explanation.definitionFit: A layshaft is a secondary shaft in a gearbox driven to carry drive between gears.

clue.text: Being a consumer, she makes short work of the opposite sex

definitions.text: she makes short work of the opposite sex

explanation.surface: A woman who consumes men and discards them quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a tiger or shark that eats people; the second a predatory woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eater is an animal that devours people, and colloquially a woman who has many lovers and discards them.

clue.text: Mother's coming between boy and girl what a bloomer!

indicators.note: coming between says one piece sits in the middle of the other two

parts.note: Michael is a boy's name
Daisy is a girl's name
mother is MA, so mother's gives MA'S

explanation.surface: A mother intervenes in a quarrel between a boy and a girl, and it ends in an embarrassing mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' reads as a blunder but means a flowering plant; the exclamation dresses it up.
explanation.definitionFit: A michaelmas daisy is an autumn-flowering aster, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Issue is dubious — 9 run out!

indicators.note: dubious suggests the remaining letters are suspect and must be rearranged
run out says the letter for run leaves the word

parts.note: 9 refers to the answer at 9 down
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a disputed issue as batsman number nine is run out.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' looks like a batting position but is the answer to 9 down, MANEATER; 'out' removes R (run) to leave MANEATE, and 'dubious' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to flow out or come forth from a source, which is what emanating means.

clue.text: Iris has a dip here in the medicinal waters

parts.note: the iris is the coloured part of the eye, standing for the whole organ
Bath is the English spa city famous for its healing hot springs

explanation.surface: A woman called Iris takes a plunge at a spa with healing waters.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a city in south-west England, known since Roman times for its mineral springs.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-bath is a small cup of lotion into which the eye is dipped for rinsing.

clue.text: Upright receiver of our confidences

explanation.surface: A trustworthy, upstanding person in whom we confide.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense rests on the saying 'between you and me and the gatepost', used when sharing a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A post at a gate stands vertical, and it is the proverbial silent witness to whispered secrets.

clue.text: An alternative, the Mahatma said, to cloth

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

indicators.note: said tells us to use the sound of the name rather than its spelling

parts.note: Mahatma Gandhi led India's independence movement

explanation.surface: A question about what Gandhi said as an alternative to wearing cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Mahatma' is Gandhi; 'said' gives only how the name is pronounced, spelt GANDIE here.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a fine, stiffened, translucent cotton fabric.

clue.text: Oral poll of employees

explanation.surface: A spoken ballot taken among the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poll' said out loud is 'pole', and a pole is a staff; the second definition is the workforce.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a pole, which is how 'poll' is pronounced, and a staff is also the body of workers in an organisation.

clue.text: Make tart flatter without cracking icing on top

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the flattery word wraps round the rest

parts.note: to adulate is to flatter excessively

indicators.note: on top points to the first letters at the head of the two words

explanation.surface: Advice for a baker: make a tart flatter without cracking the icing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside; 'on top' takes C and I, the first letters of 'cracking' and 'icing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To acidulate is to make slightly acid or sour.

clue.text: Its sprays are moist when blown about

definitions.text: Its sprays are moist when blown about

indicators.note: blown about suggests the letters scattered by the wind into a new order

explanation.surface: A scent spray releases damp droplets that drift on the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blown about' rearranges ARE and MOIST; the whole clue also describes the device.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser turns liquid into a fine mist of droplets, so its jets are damp and float off.

clue.text: X receives approval as a symbol

indicators.note: receives means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten
OK is a word of approval

explanation.surface: A mark X on a form is accepted as a sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'X' looks like a mark or a cross, but it is the Roman numeral ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A token is an object or sign standing for something else.

clue.text: One whose name is associated with a put-up job

definitions.text: One whose name is associated with a put-up job

parts.words: One whose name is associated with a put-up job
parts.note: a put-up job sounds like a fraud, but here it is a post for which someone is put up as a candidate

explanation.surface: Someone implicated in a rigged scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is a person proposed for an office, their name put forward for the post.

clue.text: Tree in Eden, one with a flower too

parts.note: Eden is the biblical garden
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A tree growing in the Garden of Eden also bears a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower too' adds that the plant is also known for its blossom; gardenias include tropical trees as well as shrubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardenia is a genus of tropical evergreen trees and shrubs with fragrant white blooms.

clue.text: Smell in river Dee said to be revealed

indicators.note: in means the smell word goes inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
hum is British slang for a bad smell

indicators.note: said means the word is heard as a sound, here a letter name

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like D

explanation.surface: A smell in the River Dee is said to have been uncovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river Dee' looks like one river, but the river is EXE and 'Dee said' is the letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhumed means dug up out of the ground, hence brought to light.

clue.text: Extremely implacable

explanation.surface: A person who is extremely unforgiving.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly is used as an intensifier, as in deadly serious, and a deadly foe is a relentless, unappeasable one.

clue.text: He usually relies on a float in his business

definitions.text: He usually relies on a float in his business

parts.words: He usually relies on a float in his business
parts.note: a float here is not a cash float or swimming aid but a small electric delivery van on British doorstep rounds

explanation.surface: A trader depends on a stock of change to run his shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A milk float is the quiet electric van British dairy deliverers drive; 'float' suggests petty cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A British doorstep dairy roundsman traditionally delivers bottles from a slow electric milk float.

clue.text: Look at the state of your pub!

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
CAL is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims over the shabby condition of a neighbourhood pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'your local' is British for the pub nearest home that one frequents.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain one's local is the nearby public house one regularly drinks at.

clue.text: Domestic belonging to an institution

explanation.surface: A household servant attached to some establishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in-house is internal, done within an organisation rather than by outsiders.

clue.text: Encounter runic enigma

indicators.note: enigma suggests a puzzle, so the letters of runic are scrambled into a riddle

explanation.surface: Coming across a puzzling ancient runic inscription.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enigma' is the anagram signal, rearranging RUNIC.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur trouble is to meet with or run into it.

clue.text: Brief spell at the top for the deputy?

parts.note: a second is a very short spell of time
someone at the top is in command

explanation.surface: A deputy gets a short stint in charge while the boss is away.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is reached playfully: a deputy holds the reins only for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: The officer next in rank below the leader acts as their deputy.

clue.text: A wave, and what makes it

explanation.surface: A wave in the sea, and the force that creates it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a hair curler, which puts a wave into hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A roller is a long heavy sea wave, and a roller is also a curler that sets waves in hair.

clue.text: Barnaby is trapped in monotonous hack work

indicators.note: is trapped in means the first piece sits enclosed by the second

parts.note: something dry is dull and monotonous
Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: A man named Barnaby is stuck in a tedious, menial job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barnaby' gives the surname RUDGE, from Dickens's novel Barnaby Rudge.
explanation.definitionFit: Drudgery is tedious, menial labour, which is what hack work is.
